title: Service Discovery
subtitle: Dynamic endpoint registration, health-checked resolution, and client-side vs server-side routing.
keyTakeaways: In containerized cloud environments, pod IP addresses are ephemeral and change constantly during autoscaling and deploys.
**Server-Side Discovery** routes requests through a virtual IP or load balancer (K8s Service / kube-proxy / ALB), keeping clients simple.
**Client-Side / Service Mesh Discovery** watches a control plane registry (xDS / Consul) and load-balances directly to pod IPs without an extra proxy hop.

sections.heading: 1. Architectural Fundamentals & Core Mechanics
sections.body: In legacy data centers, services lived on static IP addresses configured in `.ini` files. In modern cloud-native infrastructure, Kubernetes pods scale up, scale down, and reschedule across nodes every minute. **Service Discovery** maintains a real-time **Service Registry** mapping logical service names (e.g., `payment-service.prod.svc.cluster.local`) to the list of currently healthy `[IP:Port, AZ]` endpoints. Instances are registered automatically by the orchestrator (3rd-party registration pattern via Kubelet) once their Readiness probe passes, and deregistered immediately upon graceful shutdown.
bullets: **Core Architectural Principle**: In containerized cloud environments, pod IP addresses are ephemeral and change constantly during autoscaling and deploys.
**Problem Space & Invariants**: **Server-Side Discovery** routes requests through a virtual IP or load balancer (K8s Service / kube-proxy / ALB), keeping clients simple.
**System Boundary**: Operates across client network dispatch, gateway queuing, thread execution pools, and persistent storage I/O.

sections.heading: 2. Architectural Patterns & Implementation Topologies
sections.body: Distributed architectures apply specific implementation patterns and topologies for Service Discovery:
bullets: **Server-Side Discovery (AWS ALB / K8s ClusterIP)**: Provides language-agnostic; zero discovery library logic in client applications. Best suited for North-South ingress traffic and simple polyglot internal REST calls.

**Client-Side / Sidecar Mesh Discovery (gRPC xDS / Envoy)**: Provides direct pod-to-pod routing (no middle proxy hop), supports locality-aware and least-request balancing. Best suited for High-QPS East-West microservice RPC (gRPC) and multi-AZ latency-sensitive clusters.
**Self-Registration vs Third-Party Registration**: Prefer orchestrator-driven registration (Kubernetes Endpoints/EndpointSlices) over application code manually heartbeating to Eureka.
**Zone-Aware Routing (Topology Aware Hints)**: Modern discovery prioritizes endpoints in the caller's own Availability Zone (AZ) to eliminate cross-AZ bandwidth charges and cut latency by 1–2ms.

Always configure **Availability Mode (AP)** on service discovery caches: if the control plane registry goes down, clients must continue routing using their last known good cached endpoint list ('fail static').

sections.heading: 3. Production Strengths: Where & How to Apply
sections.body: Production deployments apply Service Discovery across targeted operational scenarios:
bullets: **Where to Use: High-Impact Scenarios**: Optimal for North-South ingress traffic and simple polyglot internal REST calls, suited for environments requiring Language-agnostic; zero discovery library logic in client applications.

**Where to Use: High-Throughput Scenarios**: Recommended for High-QPS East-West microservice RPC (gRPC) and multi-AZ latency-sensitive clusters, where Direct pod-to-pod routing (no middle proxy hop), supports locality-aware and least-request balancing.

**How to Use: Engineering Implementation**: In **Server-Side Discovery**, the caller sends traffic to a logical VIP/DNS backed by a load balancer (AWS ALB or Kubernetes `ClusterIP`), which forwards the packet to a healthy instance. Always establish explicit thresholds, measurement baselines, and automated monitoring.
**Architectural Leverage**: Provides predictable resource boundaries, bounds blast radius, and optimizes cost per transaction.

sections.heading: 4. Failure Modes & Trade-Offs: When to Avoid
sections.body: Improper implementation of Service Discovery introduces operational bottlenecks and failure modes:
bullets: **Where to Avoid: Trade-Off Bottlenecks**: Avoid when constraints cannot tolerate: managed l7 load balancers add an extra network hop, cost, and potential bottleneck.
**Where to Avoid: Complexity Ceiling**: Avoid when operational requirements do not justify: requires control plane infrastructure (istiod/consul) and xds state synchronization.
**Catastrophic Failure Modes**: Uncalibrated parameters can trigger queue exhaustion, thread starvation, cascading retry storms, and tail latency amplification.
**Operational Overhead**: Requires continuous observability (p95/p99 latency tracking, saturation alerts, and distributed tracing across hop boundaries).

sections.heading: 5. Staff+ Engineering Verdict & Interview Playbook
sections.body: Technical guidelines and evaluation criteria for Service Discovery:
bullets: **Staff+ Golden Rule**: **Client-Side / Service Mesh Discovery** watches a control plane registry (xDS / Consul) and load-balances directly to pod IPs without an extra proxy hop.

**Staff+ Interview Playbook**: Highlight the **gRPC L4 vs L7 load balancing trap**: a standard Kubernetes `ClusterIP` service only load-balances at L4 (TCP connection creation), so a single multiplexed HTTP/2 gRPC connection will pin 100% of requests to one pod unless you use L7 discovery (Headless Service + gRPC client balancer or Envoy).

tradeOffs.pros: Language-agnostic; zero discovery library logic in client applications.
tradeOffs.cons: Managed L7 load balancers add an extra network hop, cost, and potential bottleneck.
tradeOffs.bestFor: North-South ingress traffic and simple polyglot internal REST calls.
